trim_surface_input_group.description: Rate per LF applies to aggregate trim LF across all in-scope items. Engine sums LF from all active trim items and divides by rate to calculate hours.

task_production_rates.name: Floor Protection Setup (Perimeter Drops)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Runner-style drop cloths along trim perimeter. ~12 sec per SF. Simpler layout than full-room floor protection — runners only along active trim work areas.

task_production_rates.name: Wall Masking at Trim Edge
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape + paper masking at trim-to-wall edge for spray method. ~24 sec per LF. Brush method with SS_PAINTED_* walls uses tape-only (faster, ~200 LF/hr). Rate represents spray/paper scenario as the more labor-intensive case.
task_production_rates.state_condition_note: Spray method: always mask wall at trim edge. Brush method: mask only when walls are SS_PAINTED_*. Driven by state_declarations.adjacent_state_protection_rules for wall_field.

task_production_rates.name: Cover Fixtures Near Spray Zone
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tape over outlet/switch plates near spray zone. ~2 min per fixture.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Primer Surface

QT3.notes: Quick scan — note obvious cracked joints, missed fills

QT4.notes: Systematic inspection at 3 feet — mark all visible defects

QT5.notes: Thorough inspection under raking light — mark all imperfections

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual inspection of primed trim surfaces. QT3-QT5 rates from Fine Finish Doctrine guideline rates for inspection tasks. Inspection distance: QT3=6ft, QT4=3ft, QT5=arm's length.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Note obvious cracked joints and missed fills visible at 6 feet. Minor primer texture acceptable.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Mark all defects visible at 3 feet. Light primer texture acceptable if smooth to touch.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Mark every imperfection visible under raking light. Surface must be uniformly smooth.

task_production_rates.name: Light Sand Primer Surface
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Light sand primed trim with 150-220 grit for mechanical adhesion. ~9 sec per LF. Not removing material — creating tooth. Same process at all tiers (adhesion prep is not tiered). Per EST-006.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Caulk Cracked Joints

QT3.notes: Walk trim, caulk visible cracks only (~10% of joints). ~24 sec per LF walk rate.

QT4.notes: Walk trim, clean bead on all cracked joints (~15%). ~30 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Walk trim, perfect smooth tooled bead on all cracked joints (~20%). ~36 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Touch-up scope only — approximately 10-20% of joints need re-caulk after primer cure. Rate is per aggregate trim LF (walk rate including inspection time). Faster than full caulk job from prime spec. Per EST-006: ~150 LF/hr base.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Fill Revealed Defects

QT3.notes: Walk trim, fill obvious defects only. ~18 sec per LF.

QT4.notes: Walk trim, fill all visible defects at 3 feet. ~24 sec per LF.

QT5.notes: Walk trim, fill every defect that could telegraph through finish. ~28 sec per LF.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spot fill defects revealed after primer cure. Walk rate including inspection time. Lighter scope than prime spec heavy fill. Per EST-006: ~200 LF/hr base.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Sanding Dust (Initial Prep)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe all trim surfaces. ~6 sec per LF. Quick pass — same pace at all tiers. Per EST-006.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat 1
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush finish coat 1. ~45 sec per LF. Coat 1 is slower than coat 2 (surface absorption, establishing coverage). Apply, tip once, walk away — short working time demands proper first-pass technique (FFD 15.3.1). Per EST-001/EST-007.

defect_tolerance.QT3: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Light brush texture acceptable if it won't telegraph after next coat.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Minimal brush texture — will sand between coats.
defect_tolerance.QT5: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Zero brush marks — any remaining texture will be sanded out with 220-320 grit.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat 1
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray finish coat 1 (310-411 tip). ~9.5 sec per LF. Coat 1 slower than coat 2 (establishing coverage). Consistent distance and speed for uniform mil thickness. Per EST-001/EST-007.

defect_tolerance.QT3: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. No orange peel. Uniform mil thickness.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. No orange peel. Uniform coverage.
defect_tolerance.QT5: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. No orange peel. Perfect uniform coverage — any defect sanded out between coats.

task_production_rates.name: Inspect Coat (Interstage)

QT3.notes: Quick glance at 6 feet — obvious defects only

QT4.notes: Systematic scan at 3 feet — mark all visible defects

QT5.notes: Lighted critical inspection at arm's length — zero tolerance

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Visual inspection of applied coat for dust nibs, brush marks, missed areas, runs, texture issues. Rates from Fine Finish Doctrine guideline: QT3=800, QT4=500, QT5=300 LF/hr. Per EST-001.

defect_tolerance.QT3: Flag obvious defects: runs, sags, holidays, dust nibs visible at 6 feet. Minor brush texture or orange peel acceptable if coat 2 will cover.
defect_tolerance.QT4: Flag all defects visible at 3 feet. Minor surface texture acceptable only if it will sand out cleanly.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Flag every imperfection at arm's length under work light. Nothing carries forward to next coat.

task_production_rates.name: Sand Between Coats

QT3.notes: Spot sand only — visible nibs and rough spots. 220 grit.

QT4.notes: Light full sand — entire surface, 220 grit. Uniform scratch pattern.

QT5.notes: Thorough full sand — entire surface, 220-320 grit. Every imperfection addressed.

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Between-coat sanding with rigid sanding block (FFD 15.4.1). QT3 spot sand only. QT4 full surface 220 grit. QT5 full surface 220-320 grit. Rates from Fine Finish Doctrine guideline: QT3=400, QT4=250, QT5=150 LF/hr. Per EST-001.

task_production_rates.name: Patch/Repair Defects (Interstage)

QT3.notes: Repair glaring defects only — deep scratches, obvious holes

QT4.notes: Repair all marked defects — visible at 3 feet

QT5.notes: Repair all defects regardless of size — anything that could telegraph through finish

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Spot fill/patch defects found during interstage inspection. Walk rate — most LF requires no patching at QT3, increasing scope at higher tiers. Per EST-001: ~400 LF/hr base.

task_production_rates.name: Spot Coat Patched Areas

QT5.notes: Spot coat all repairs — ensure uniform film build

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Apply spot coat over patched/repaired areas. Walk rate — scope proportional to patch scope. Per EST-001: ~500 LF/hr base.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Sanding Dust (Interstage)
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Tack cloth wipe all sanded trim surfaces between coats. ~6 sec per LF. Same pace at all tiers — complete dust removal is binary.

task_production_rates.name: Brush Finish Coat 2
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Brush finish coat 2. ~40 sec per LF. Faster than coat 1 — consistent substrate, no absorption. Same application philosophy: apply, tip once, walk away. Also used for coat 3 at QT5 brush/roll. Per EST-001/EST-007.

defect_tolerance.QT3: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Uniform coverage and sheen.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Uniform sheen across all surfaces.
defect_tolerance.QT5: No drips, sags, holidays, or lap marks. Perfect uniform sheen — zero brush marks.

task_production_rates.name: Spray Finish Coat 2
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Airless spray finish coat 2. ~8 sec per LF. Faster than coat 1 — consistent substrate. Per EST-001/EST-007.

defect_tolerance.QT3: No drips, sags, holidays. No orange peel. Uniform coverage.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No drips, sags, holidays. No orange peel. Uniform sheen.
defect_tolerance.QT5: No drips, sags, holidays. No orange peel. Perfect uniform coverage and sheen.

task_production_rates.name: Final Trim Inspection

QT3.notes: Quick glance at 6 feet — no obvious defects

QT4.notes: Systematic scan at 3 feet — no visible defects, uniform sheen

QT5.notes: Critical inspection at arm's length under raking light — zero tolerance, uniform sheen across all surfaces

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Final quality check of all painted trim surfaces. Verify coverage uniformity, sheen consistency, defect-free finish. Research baseline 600 LF/hr at QT3. Slower than interstage inspect (800) because final inspection is more thorough even at QT3. Per EST-001.

defect_tolerance.QT3: No obvious defects at 6 feet. Uniform sheen across each trim type. Minor texture variations acceptable between different trim profiles.
defect_tolerance.QT4: No visible defects at 3 feet. Uniform sheen across all surfaces. Consistent finish quality between trim types.
defect_tolerance.QT5: Zero defects at arm's length under raking light. Perfectly uniform sheen across all surfaces. No texture variation. Gallery-quality finish.

task_production_rates.name: Touch-Up Defects (Final)

QT4.notes: Address all visible defects — blend touch-up into surrounding finish

QT5.notes: Address every imperfection — full coat over spot repairs if needed to equalize sheen

task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Touch-up defects found during final inspection. Walk rate with spot work. QT5 may require full coat over repair areas to equalize sheen. Per EST-001: ~400 LF/hr base.

task_production_rates.name: Protection Teardown
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Remove all protection: floor drops, wall masking tape/paper, fixture covers. Rate based on floor protection SF (primary zone). Teardown is ~1.5x faster than setup — picking up drops is faster than placing them. Wall/fixture teardown bundled into rate. Remove tape while finish is slightly tacky for clean edge.

task_production_rates.name: Clean Tools
task_production_rates.rate_basis_notes: Fixed time: ~30 min per session regardless of trim quantity. Clean brushes, spray equipment (if used). All waterborne products — water cleanup. Proper storage or disposal of consumables.

quality_tier_effects.description: Standard trim finish painting — baseline for all rates
quality_tier_effects.notes: Standard NC production pace. Per Modifier_Registry QT3_STANDARD = 1.00. Application quality is identical at all tiers — QT3 saves time on inspection scrutiny, sanding discipline (spot only), and repair scope (glaring defects only). Coat count: 2 finish coats.

quality_tier_effects.description: Premium trim finish painting — thorough prep, full sand between coats
quality_tier_effects.notes: Per Modifier_Registry QT4_PREMIUM = 1.30. Applied to qt_scaled tasks via explicit qt_rates. Sanding: full 220 grit entire surface. Inspection: systematic at 3 feet. Repair: all visible defects. Coat count: 2 finish coats. Semi-gloss minimum sheen.

quality_tier_effects.description: Superior trim finish painting — maximum care, zero tolerance
quality_tier_effects.notes: Per Modifier_Registry QT5_SUPERIOR = 1.50. Applied to qt_scaled tasks via explicit qt_rates. Sanding: thorough 220-320 grit. Inspection: critical at arm's length under raking light. Repair: all defects regardless of size. Coat count: 2 coats (spray) or 3+ coats (brush/roll per FFD 15.10.3). Gloss sheen allowed.

additional_rounds.description: QT5 brush/roll adds coat 3 + interstage 2. Coat 3 uses TSK_TRIM_BRUSH_FINISH_2 rates (consistent substrate). Per FFD 15.10.3 and human resolution (Brief Q3).
additional_rounds.notes: Do NOT enforce spray for QT5 gloss — brush/roll is achievable with proper technique and additional coats.

profile_complexity_modifiers.notes: 15% time reduction. Simple profiles paint and sand faster. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 7.2.

profile_complexity_modifiers.description: Ogee, cove, or standard residential profiles

profile_complexity_modifiers.notes: 25% time increase. More edges, crevices, detail work per LF. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 7.2.

profile_complexity_modifiers.description: Dentil, egg-and-dart, or highly detailed profiles
profile_complexity_modifiers.notes: 40% time increase. Maximum detail density per LF. Per Millwork_NC_Paint_Doctrine Section 7.2.

height_access_effects.description: Standard 7-8 ft working height (baseboard, door/window casing, chair rail)
height_access_effects.notes: Floor-level access. Baseline. Most trim types. Per Modifier_Registry H1_STANDARD = 1.00.

height_access_effects.description: Tall 9-12 ft working height (crown molding, high casings, picture rail)
height_access_effects.notes: Step/extension ladder required. Primarily affects crown molding and upper trim. Per Modifier_Registry H2_TALL = 1.30.
Scaffold likely required. Rare for standard residential trim. Per Modifier_Registry H3_HIGH = 1.50.

crew_configurations.name: Single Trim Brush Painter
crew_configurations.notes: One skilled painter brushes all trim types. Works systematically by room, by trim type within each room. May need helper for protection setup.

crew_configurations.name: Single Trim Sprayer
crew_configurations.notes: One sprayer handles all trim types. Helper recommended for masking/protection setup. Sprayer focuses on application only.

rate_notes.multi_surface_aggregation: This spec covers 9 trim types, all measured in LF. Production rates apply per LF regardless of which trim type the footage comes from. The engine sums LF from all in-scope trim items and divides by the task rate to calculate hours. Profile complexity modifiers are applied per-item (baseboard may be 'simple' while crown may be 'complex' in the same room).
rate_notes.coat_1_vs_coat_2: Coat 1 is systematically slower than coat 2. Coat 1: surface absorption, establishing coverage, first-pass onto sanded primer. Coat 2: consistent substrate, known absorption, faster pace. Separate task IDs (TSK_TRIM_BRUSH_FINISH_1 vs _2) enable distinct rates. Coat 3 at QT5 uses coat 2 rates.
rate_notes.modifier_application: Modifiers increase TIME, not rate. effective_rate = base_rate / modifier. Modifiers stack multiplicatively: total_modifier = profile_complexity x height x QT (for qt_scaled tasks). Application task rates (brush/spray finish) are NOT modified by QT — application quality is binary, not tiered.
rate_notes.pca_measurement_note: Per PCA standards, surfaces <1 ft width are measured as 1 LF regardless of actual width. A 3-inch baseboard and 6-inch crown are equivalent from a production measurement perspective. Profile complexity modifiers account for actual work differences.

assumptions.value: Initial prep tasks (caulk, fill, sand) are faster than prime spec equivalents because scope is touch-up only (~10-15% of joints/defects need rework)
assumptions.note: No doctrine defines finish vs prime prep rate ratios. Derived from research and practical scope reduction.

assumptions.value: qt_scaled tasks use explicit per-tier rates rather than mechanical QT modifier division because scope genuinely changes (not just pace)
assumptions.source: Fine Finish Doctrine guideline rates, research EST-004
assumptions.note: Inspection goes from glance to meticulous. Sanding goes from spot to full surface. Repair goes from glaring to everything. Scope changes create non-linear scaling.

assumptions.value: Coat 3 at QT5 brush/roll uses same rates as coat 2 (TSK_TRIM_BRUSH_FINISH_2 at 90 LF/hr)
assumptions.note: No separate coat 3 rate defined. Coat 2 rates apply — substrate is consistent after first coat.

assumptions.value: Protection teardown modeled as single task with SF-based rate, bundling floor/wall/fixture teardown
assumptions.note: Practical simplification. Teardown rate based on floor protection SF as primary zone. Wall and fixture teardown adds ~15% overhead bundled into rate.

validation_plan.method: Time painter brushing 100 LF baseboard (standard profile) across multiple rooms
validation_plan.notes: Verify coat 1 vs coat 2 rate differential. Time both passes separately.

validation_plan.method: Time sprayer coating 500 LF mixed trim (baseboard + casing) in production setting
validation_plan.notes: Verify coat 1 vs coat 2 differential. Exclude masking time (separate task).

validation_plan.method: Time same painter sanding 50 LF at QT3 (spot) vs QT4 (full) vs QT5 (thorough)
validation_plan.notes: Verify that scope change (spot vs full) creates expected rate differential.

validation_plan.method: Compare production times for 50 LF simple baseboard vs 50 LF ornate crown
validation_plan.notes: Verify complexity modifiers against field data.

validation_plan.method: Count cracked joints on 3 completed prime jobs, measure actual rework percentage
validation_plan.expected_range: 10-20% of joints need touch-up after primer cure
validation_plan.notes: Validates assumption about touch-up scope reduction vs full caulk.
